scope.requirements: raffle.fun non-upgradeable ERC-721 prize raffle protocol (Raffle.sol, RaffleFactory.sol, IRaffle.sol, IRaffleFactory.sol, RaffleConstants.sol). Requirements: (1) Never move assets between raffle clones or lock assets in protocol sinks; (2) Escrowed prizeToken must be verified and isolated per raffle; (3) Ticket entries are fixed 1 USDC (6 decimals), sequential 1-indexed contiguous ranges [startEntry, endEntry], transferable via ERC-721; (4) Chainlink VRF v2.5 Direct Funding native wrapper draw within [endTime, endTime + 2 days) and callback within [requestedAt, requestedAt + 2 days); (5) Settlement is permissionless and storage-only, splitting 95% sponsor / 5% treasury on NftWon (totalEntries >= reserveEntries) or 80% winner / 15% sponsor / 5% treasury on CashWon (totalEntries < reserveEntries); (6) Pull-claim isolation for winner redemption, sponsor proceeds, sponsor prize reclaim, protocol fees, and ticket refunds.

findings.title: Predictable CREATE clone addresses bypass _isProtocolDestination before deployment, locking quote payouts and allowing cross-clone prize transfers
findings.description:
RaffleFactory.createRaffle deploys clones with Clones.clone(raffleImplementation) (EVM CREATE opcode), making every future clone address deterministic from (address(factory), nonce). Before a future clone R_future is deployed, R_future.code.length == 0 and canonicalFactory.isRaffle(R_future) == false. Consequently, R_future passes RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams and Raffle._isProtocolDestination during Raffle.initialize (as sponsorRecipient) and Raffle._update (as a ticket recipient in buyEntries or transferFrom), and bypasses ERC721Utils.checkOnERC721Received. Once R_future is deployed by a subsequent createRaffle call, isRaffle[R_future] becomes true and R_future.code.length == 45: (1) Raffle.releaseSponsorProceeds calls _transferQuote(R_future, amount), which re-checks _isProtocolDestination and permanently reverts with InvalidQuoteDestination(R_future), locking sponsorProceeds; (2) Raffle.releaseSponsorPrize and Raffle.redeemWinningTicket (in Status.NftWon) omit _isProtocolDestination and call prizeToken.transferFrom(address(this), R_future, prizeTokenId), moving the prize NFT into clone R_future in violation of the cross-clone asset isolation invariant and stranding the NFT permanently; (3) any ticket owned by R_future can never be redeemed or refunded because Raffle has no outbound call to redeemWinningTicket or refundTickets; (4) if protocolTreasury is configured to a future clone CREATE address R_k in the RaffleFactory constructor, createRaffle permanently reverts at raffle k with UnsafeProtocolDestination.
Assumptions: A caller or sponsor specifies a precomputed future CREATE address of RaffleFactory before that clone index is deployed.; At least one subsequent createRaffle call occurs to deploy the clone at that predicted address.

findings.title: Decoupled sponsorProceeds payout in Status.NftWon allows sponsor to claim 95% of buyer USDC even when prizeToken delivery fails in redeemWinningTicket
findings.description:
In Status.NftWon, _settleWinningTicket allocates 95% of unsettledPot to sponsorProceeds and 5% to protocolFees in storage without transferring prizeToken or verifying that prizeToken remains transferable to the winning ticket owner. Raffle.releaseSponsorProceeds only checks sponsorProceeds != 0 and does not require prizeClaimed == true when status == Status.NftWon. If the arbitrary ERC-721 prizeToken is pausable, blacklist-enabled, expiring, soulbound-after-escrow, or sponsor-controlled and reverts (or fails the post-transfer ownerOf check) during redeemWinningTicket, the sponsor still extracts 95% of buyer USDC while the winner cannot receive the NFT and the raffle cannot transition from Status.NftWon to Status.Refunding.
Assumptions: The escrowed prizeToken is an arbitrary ERC-721 contract that succeeds during createRaffle safeTransferFrom but reverts or blocks transfer when redeemWinningTicket is called after settlement.

findings.title: Discontinuous payout cliff at reserveEntries and unrestricted single-buyer under-target draw enable sponsor self-purchase arbitrage and 20% fee extraction
findings.description:
When totalEntries crosses reserveEntries, settlement switches discontinuously from Status.CashWon (80% winnerProceeds, 15% sponsorProceeds, 5% protocolFees, plus prize NFT returned to sponsor) to Status.NftWon (0% winnerProceeds, 95% sponsorProceeds, 5% protocolFees). Because neither sponsor nor sponsorRecipient is blocked in buyEntries, a sponsor receives a 95% rebate on every entry bought once totalEntries >= reserveEntries (paying $0.05 net per $1.00 entry) and can buy the shortfall right before endTime to capture 80% of existing buyers' pot plus proportional probability of winning back the NFT. Conversely, when totalEntries < reserveEntries and only a single buyer (or single ticket) participated, requestDraw can still be called at endTime to force Status.CashWon, extracting 15% sponsorProceeds + 5% protocolFees from the sole buyer while returning the NFT to the sponsor.
Assumptions: Economic mechanism treats sponsor entries identically to external buyer entries and permits draws when ticketCount == 1 below reserveEntries.

findings.title: Sponsor pre-endTime empty-raffle cancellation in enableRefunds can be front-run by a 1-USDC buyEntries transaction
findings.description:
Raffle.enableRefunds allows the sponsor to cancel an active raffle before endTime only when totalEntries == 0. Because buyEntries is permissionless while block.timestamp < endTime, an observer in the public mempool can front-run the sponsor's enableRefunds() call with buyEntries(recipient, 1) for 1 USDC (1e6 quoteToken units). This increments totalEntries to 1, causing the sponsor's enableRefunds() transaction to take the totalEntries != 0 branch and revert with RefundsNotAvailable(endTime + 2 days, block.timestamp), locking the prize NFT until at least endTime (and winning the NFT for 1 USDC if reserveEntries == 1).
Assumptions: The sponsor broadcasts enableRefunds() via a public mempool before endTime while totalEntries == 0.

findings.title: Untrusted prizeToken.safeTransferFrom in createRaffle activates the Raffle clone before RaffleCreated is emitted and before post-transfer ownerOf verification
findings.description:
In RaffleFactory.createRaffle, prize.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, raffle, params.prizeTokenId) invokes Raffle.onERC721Received, which transitions the clone from Status.Initialized to Status.Active and emits PrizeDeposited before safeTransferFrom returns to RaffleFactory. Because Raffle's own ReentrancyGuard is not entered during createRaffle, a custom or hook-enabled prizeToken contract can call raffle.buyEntries(recipient, entryCount) inside safeTransferFrom after onERC721Received returns, emitting Transfer and TicketPurchased events before RaffleFactory verifies prize.ownerOf(params.prizeTokenId) == raffle and before RaffleCreated is emitted.
Assumptions: The prizeToken contract executes an external call to the newly created Raffle clone inside safeTransferFrom after calling onERC721Received.

findings.title: Unbounded reserveEntries upper limit, unrestricted secondary ticket transfers during Status.Drawing, and ERC-1167 ReentrancyGuard cold-slot gas overhead
findings.description:
Three defense-in-depth and gas hygiene issues exist across RaffleFactory and Raffle: (1) RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams only checks reserveEntries != 0 and enforces no upper bound on uint128 reserveEntries, allowing raffles where reserveEntries exceeds total USDC supply so Status.NftWon is unreachable; (2) Raffle._update does not restrict ERC-721 ticket transfers during Status.Drawing or after draw fulfillment, exposing open secondary-market orders or bids on tickets to mempool front-running once the VRF fulfillment transaction is visible; (3) Raffle inherits storage-backed ReentrancyGuard (where _status starts at 0 in uninitialized ERC-1167 clone storage rather than _NOT_ENTERED = 1), charging the first buyEntries caller a 20,000-gas 0-to-1 SSTORE penalty, and hardcodes VRF_CALLBACK_GAS_LIMIT = 300_000 even though fulfillRandomWords only writes 4 storage slots.
Assumptions: Target EVM is cancun (as configured in foundry.toml), where transient storage (EIP-1153) is available.
